tara_cust: Heads up — after the 10% canary yesterday we started seeing our assistant flip answers mid-conversation. Same session, same prompt, different facts in the same turn. Happening ~8% of sessions. Example below.

alex_support: Ugh. Can you paste a minimal repro (transcript + request headers/x-ids) and confirm hosted/dedicated/private? Also need timestamps.

tara_cust: Hosted (api.redwood.ai). Minimal transcript and headers: 
```
User: "List the 3 changes to the SLA in plain bullets."
AI (reply A): "- Removal of 30-day grace period; customers must provide 30-day notice."
AI (reply B, same turn): "No SLA changes; current terms unchanged."
```
No parallel requests on our side, session token same. Request headers we captured: x-request-id: req-cc7a4a, session-id: s-zz987, x-client-tag: web-frontend. Streaming observed a short pause then resumed with different wording.

Curl:
```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-..." -H "X-Session-ID: s-zz987" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-stable","input":"List the 3 changes to the SLA in plain bullets.","stream":true}'
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-15T09:08:12Z

alex_support: Thanks. Escalating to oncall/runtime. @sana_oncall can you pull routing and stream logs for req-cc7a4a and check variant assignments and any fallback events? Also ping @deploy_bot for rollouts around 09:00Z.

sana_oncall: Pulled logs. Route shows initial assignment to variant "q4-small-v2" then a fallback at +96ms to "base-fp16-v1" with reason: "pool_overcommitted". Stream log shows chunk boundary at byte offset 512 where worker switch occurred. Routing excerpt:
```
[09:08:12.000] route req-cc7a4a -> pool:gpu-small variant:q4-small-v2 worker:gpu-07
[09:08:12.096] fallback req-cc7a4a -> pool:gpu-large variant:base-fp16-v1 reason:pool_overcommitted
[09:08:12.097] stream_resume req-cc7a4a -> worker:gpu-21 offset:512
```

deploy_bot: Canary redwood-chat-stable -> base-fp16-v1 rolled to 12% at 2026-03-15T08:50:00Z; autoscale bump at 09:05Z.

sana_oncall: Root cause: fallback allowed mid-stream. When we switch workers/variants mid-stream we may not preserve sampler/state so outputs can diverge. That explains contradictory facts.

eng-runtime: This is a known low-frequency edge case. Two immediate mitigation options: 1) enforce session affinity for lifespan of session (pin variant at session start), or 2) fail the stream on fallback (return non-200 so client can retry). Both have tradeoffs.

product_pm: For customer-facing guidance, we should recommend a pinned session header and offer tenant pinning as short-term workaround. Also publish a FAQ and SDK retry behavior.

alex_support: @tara_cust two options for now: (A) we can temporarily pin your tenant to base-fp16-v1 for N hours; (B) leave traffic as-is and we will notify you of possible inconsistency windows during canary/scale events. Which do you want?

tara_cust: Please pin us to base-fp16-v1 for 48h. Also, what response headers should we log to detect this if it happens again?

alex_support: Use these response headers to detect a mid-stream handoff: `x-request-id`, `x-variant-id`, `x-fallback-reason`, `x-stream-resume-offset`. Example when fallback happens:
```
x-request-id: req-cc7a4a
x-variant-id: base-fp16-v1
x-fallback-reason: pool_overcommitted
x-stream-resume-offset: 512
```

sana_oncall: Tenant pin applied: tenant T-4123 pinned to base-fp16-v1 for 48h. Monitoring metrics flagged. Also created ephemeral flag for strict session-affinity to enable on canary lanes.

eng-runtime: Action items noted: 
- P1: return 409 Conflict on mid-stream variant handoff instead of silently resuming (owner: sana_oncall) ETA 72h
- P1: add tenant/session pinning API + doc (owner: eng-runtime) ETA 48h
- P2: SDK auto-retry on 409 + doc (owner: devex) ETA 7d
- P3: long-term: safe state transfer/KV rehydration on handoff (owner: eng-runtime-research) ETA TBD

product_pm: We'll send an advisory to affected customers and add an FAQ item about variant-pinning and 409 semantics.

alex_support: @tara_cust we've pinned you. Please watch for any further mixed answers and paste new examples if you see them. Appreciate the detailed repro.

tara_cust: Thanks everyone. We'll monitor and share any further traces. Logging the headers now. :thumbsup:
